sentences.text: Velocipes means "quick foot" and is a Late Triassic saurischian dinosaur that may have been a theropod.
The surviving fibula fragment is 16.4 cm long, suggesting the full bone was roughly 30-35 cm.
This bone features a concave medial surface and a lateral ridge measuring about 52 mm long and 5 mm high.
Based on the fibula size, Velocipes may have reached up to 3 meters long and weighed around 50 kg, though this is speculative due to the single known specimen.
The type species Velocipes guerichi was first described by Huene in 1932 based on a poorly preserved fibula discovered in southern Poland around 1884.
The fossil bone was described but not named until 1884.
The fossil bone was thought to be destroyed after damage during World War II until it was rediscovered in 2012.
Recent studies consider Velocipes to be a basal neotheropod or closely related to that clade.
Velocipes lived alongside the aetosaur Kocurypelta, an indeterminate lungfish, and the stem-turtle Proterochersis.
In 1956, Velocipes was placed in the Halticosauridae, a family that later became monotypic.
Velocipes fossils were found in the Norian-aged Lissauer Breccia of southern Poland.
Velocipes lived during the Norian stage, between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
In 1984, Samuel Paul Welles suggested that Velocipes might be synonymous with Liliensternus.
